Infrastructure and industrial projects worth nearly $2 trillion underpin demand, while GCC crude steel production rose 9.5% in 2025

Staff Writer ,  TradeArabia

 The Middle East is an increasingly important market for global steel, underpinned by nearly $2 trillion in infrastructure and industrial projects and a market forecast to grow from $44 billion in 2026 to $60 billion by 2031. 

At a time when steel producers worldwide are navigating shifting trade flows, evolving decarbonisation requirements and ongoing market uncertainty, leaders from across the steel value chain will gather at Fastmarkets’ Middle East Iron & Steel (MEIS) 2026 in Dubai this November to assess the region's growth, trade and investment outlook.

Regional host sponsor EMSTEEL’s Group CEO, Eng Saeed Ghumran Al Remeithi, will be joined by senior industry figures including Ahmed Ezz, CEO of Ezz Steel; Sharjeel Azhar, CEO of Al Ittefaq Steel Products; Dr Salam Al Sharif, Chairman of Al Sharif Metals Group & BMR; Sanjay Roychoudhury, CEO of UNICOIL and Jose Noldin, CEO of GravitHY.

Region's momentum

The region's momentum is reflected in production. According to Fastmarkets analysis, GCC crude steel output reached 21.6 million tonnes in 2025, up 9.5% year over year. Electric arc furnaces account for approximately 95% of regional crude steel production, giving the Middle East a strong position in the transition to lower-carbon steelmaking.

"The past year has been challenging for many parts of the steel industry, making it more important than ever to focus on where real opportunities are emerging," said Raju Daswani, CEO of Fastmarkets. "The Middle East combines significant investment, growing demand, ambitious industrial development and a strong position in lower-carbon steelmaking. MEIS brings the industry together to build relationships, identify commercial opportunities and better understand where this market is heading."

“The Middle East is moving from ambition to delivery, supported by major investments in infrastructure, manufacturing and industrial development,” said Eng Saeed Ghumran Al Remeithi, Group CEO of EMSTEEL. “At EMSTEEL, our focus is to support this growth with reliable, high-quality steel while accelerating the transition towards lower-carbon production. The region has the resources, capabilities and determination to play an increasingly important role in the future of the global steel industry.”

Forces reshaping regional steel markets

MEIS 2026 will examine the forces reshaping regional steel markets, including major infrastructure and industrial projects, steel demand, trade flows, tariffs, carbon regulation and the security of supply for key raw materials such as scrap, DR-grade iron ore, pellets, DRI and HBI.

Middle East Iron & Steel 2026 takes place from November 16 to 18 at Madinat Jumeirah, Dubai.—TradeArabia News Service
